description: Expectations for the UML3 sample (samples/uml3) drawn as diagrams in CATIA Magic and exported to SVG and PNG (E23; tools/check_view_svg.py, cameo_check.py --sample-svg). Recorded 2026-09-24 from the first run, whose predictions are in tests/cameo-experiments/e23-predictions.json. The point of these expectations is that the sample says nothing about how to draw it: every shape is there because a UML3 keyword put it there, so a change that breaks the keyword-to-diagram correspondence shows up here. Unlike svg-expectations.json these views name their includes and excludes directly, because the sample has no separate prediction file.

views.comment: The 11 elements ClassDiagram selects, one compact box each. The 4 enumeration literals are drawn inside OrderStatus and are not listed: they are not exposed elements. The sample's 2 dependencies are unnamed, so they can be neither included nor excluded by name; E23 P5 records that CATIA Magic draws dependencies as edges.

The same 11 elements with their compartments, so the features are asserted too: this is where the model's detail is proved. isPaid is excluded because CATIA Magic draws no calculation compartment, so a '#query calc' is invisible (E23 P11, issue I-41) - it is a defect recorded as an expectation, not a filter doing its job, and this line should be deleted when a calc becomes visible.

ClassTable selects classifiers only. The excludes are the whole point of this view: the exception, the association and the composition have their own keywords and must not appear, which is what tells ClassTable apart from ClassDiagram over the same package.
